summary: An ox killed a cow, and a dead calf is found next to it. We don't know if the calf was born before or after, so the owner pays half for the cow and a quarter for the calf. The same kind of rule works when the cow did the goring.

chunks.st: In the case of an innocuous ox that gored and killed a cow,

chunks.st: or whether it gave birth after the ox gored it and the fetus died on account of the goring,

chunks.explain: Since we are not sure, he pays half of half.
chunks.st: and one-quarter of the cost of the damage for the offspring.
chunks.stMore: Since it is uncertain whether the ox was responsible for the death of the fetus, in which case he would pay half the damages, its owner pays only half the amount for the fetus that he would ordinarily be required to pay, i.e., one-quarter.

chunks.st: or whether the cow gave birth after it gored.
chunks.stMore: When damage is caused by an innocuous animal, the liability of the owner is limited to the value of the animal that gored.

chunks.en: he is paid half damage from the cow
chunks.st: Therefore, half the cost of the damage is paid from the value of the cow, as in the standard case of an innocuous animal.

chunks.en: and a quarter damage from the calf.
chunks.st: And if that does not suffice to pay for half the cost of the damage, one-quarter of the cost of the damage is paid from the offspring.
chunks.stMore: Since it is uncertain whether the offspring was part of the cow at the time the cow gored, the owner pays only half of what he would pay if it were certain that it was part of the cow.
